# Juniper SRX System Health and Chassis Cluster

_Juniper SRX · 16 commands_

Operational health checks for standalone and clustered SRX. Version and uptime, hardware and alarms, CPU and memory, storage and core dumps, cluster state, and data for a JTAC case.

## Details

### `show system uptime`

An unexpected recent boot time points to a crash or power loss; check `show system core-dumps` next.


### `show chassis alarms / show system alarms`

Both lists should be empty on a healthy box. A missing rescue configuration also raises a system alarm.


### `show chassis routing-engine`

This is the control plane. Forwarding load (SPU or flow CPU) is shown by `show security monitoring`.


### `show system processes extensive`

```
show system processes extensive | no-more
```


### `show security monitoring`

High flow CPU or a session table near its maximum explains drops even when routing and policies are correct.


### `show security flow session summary`

Many failed sessions point to policy or resource problems; filters such as `destination-prefix <ip>` also work with summary.


### `show system storage`

`request system storage cleanup dry-run` lists what a cleanup would delete (old logs, core files, images) without deleting anything.


### `request support information | save /var/tmp/rsi-<date>.txt`

Run it before a reboot, while the problem is still there, and attach the file together with /var/log to the case.


### `show chassis cluster status [redundancy-group <n>]`

RG0 is the Routing Engine (control plane), RG1 and higher carry the reth interfaces (data plane). A priority of 0 means a monitored interface or IP failed on that node. A node shown as lost or disabled points to a control or fabric link problem.


### `show chassis cluster interfaces`

Control and fabric links must be up; if both fail, the nodes can end up split-brain.


### `show chassis cluster statistics`

Increasing errors or missed heartbeats on the control link precede failovers.


### `show chassis cluster information`

The first place to look when you want to know why a failover happened.
